features.feature_value: Used post wording (civil/educational vs accusatory) and imagined conversational interpretation to decide keep/remove
features.evidence_span: What influenced me the most in my evaluations was the wording of the posts.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states wording and perceived tone/impact in conversation were the main influence.

features.feature_value: Treated vulgar swearing and name-calling as grounds for removal and non-productive comments as unneeded
features.evidence_span: Vulgar, swearing language is an automatic removal. As well as most name-calling and non-productive comments is highly unneeded.
features.rationale: The participant gives explicit thresholds (automatic removal) tied to profanity and name-calling.

features.feature_value: Removal driven primarily by heavy curse words/excessive vulgar language
features.evidence_span: I was trying remove the posts that heavily used curse words or contained excessive vulgar language
features.rationale: Their reflection centers the removal criterion on vulgar language.

features.feature_value: Stated broad permissiveness, mainly restricting content that directly calls for violence or directly harms/targets individuals or groups
features.evidence_span: anyone should be able to say almost anything as long as it doesn't directly call for violence or directly harmfully target a certain individual or group of people.
features.rationale: They specify an exception-based rule for removal while allowing most other viewpoints.

features.feature_value: Supports free speech/dissent and doesn't mind foul language; removed only content described as conspiracy-like and inciting violence
features.evidence_span: I don't mind dissenting opinions or foul language. I only removed the last two and it was because the 19th felt conspiracy theory-ish and the 20th was inciting violence.
features.rationale: They link their specific removals to conspiracy framing and violence incitement while endorsing speech broadly.

features.feature_value: Checked whether language was hurtful vs merely opinion and preferred less aggressive pairs to avoid creating another way people get hurt
features.evidence_span: the first thing I checked was langauge and if it was hurtful or just simply being an opinion. i also picked the less agressive pairs
features.rationale: They describe a pair-based comparison approach (less aggressive pairing) driven by perceived hurtfulness.

features.feature_value: Said the pair didn't seem like true mirrors; used perceived abuse asymmetry (right righteous indignation vs left abusive for fun) and removed overly abusive posts

features.feature_value: Focused on validity of arguments and accuracy/understanding to decide keep/remove
